platform_note: This one-shot is a **humanoid** example. Reuse the same critique→config discipline on every robot platform (tiago, roomba, quadruped, single_arm): Recognition / Correction Q1 / Q2 must drive large, iconic parameter changes — not tiny pose polish.
description: Theatrical lion roar: wide claw hands high and forward, then aggressive shoulder-z beats.
recognition_q: A robot crouches down and then stands up.
correction_q1: no, The motion lacks any distinct "lion" characteristics like claws or a roar; it's just a generic crouch and stand.
correction_q2: The entire motion needs to be redesigned to be more theatrical: start in a low crouch with wide, claw-like hands, then have the robot explode upwards, throwing its head back forcefully and thrusting its arms forward to simulate a powerful roar.

origin.label: prior attempt (failed — generic crouch/stand)
origin.source_code: pose(dir=front, grip=vert, torso=low, z=45, x=65, left_arm=mirror) + move(torso, height, high, spd=3.0) + move(head, tilt, -30, spd=3.0, hold=0.8)

corrected.label: corrected attempt (implements Q2 with bold margins)
corrected.source_code: pose(dir=front, grip=horiz, x=80, y=30, z=80, left_arm=mirror) + move(shoulder, z, 30, spd=1.5, rep=1) + move(shoulder, z, -60, spd=3.5, rep=1)

lesson: Q2 said thrust arms forward / theatrical roar — so the rewrite jumps x=65→80, z=45→80, y=50→30 (wide claws) and adds large shoulder-z beats at spd=1.5 then 3.5. +z raises the hands, −z lowers them (world-axis signed). Do not answer Q2 with only ±5 percentile polish.
